content: Patients classified under Category 0, who are at very low risk with no evidence of loss of protective sensation (LOPS) or peripheral arterial disease (PAD), should undergo a foot examination once per year. Patients in Category 1, identified as low risk due to the presence of either LOPS or PAD, should have their feet examined every 6 to 12 months. Patients in Category 2, considered at moderate risk because they exhibit both LOPS and PAD or have foot deformities, should receive a foot examination every 3 to 6 months. Patients in Category 3, categorized as high risk due to a history of foot ulceration or amputation, should have their feet examined at intervals of every 1 to 3 months.
